## TL;DR

I ran a QA pass over Settings → Notifications (ntfy, the Telegram bot section, and per-chat task notifications) and fixed what it found. Round 1 fixed the copy, error states and dialogs on those screens. Review round 1 then showed that I had fixed only the instances the first pass named, so this round fixes every sibling of each bug: three more `...JSON_OPTS` spreads and five more native `confirm()` calls across the UI. A source-scan guard now fails on either pattern anywhere in `ui-app/src`. The QA findings are in `docs/qa/2026-11-notifications-qa.md`. Nothing contacts Telegram, no real token is used, and no token appears in the rendered page. Human checks remain: a real bot, and an ntfy test delivered to a phone.

## Work and rationale

Round 1 covered the three components the task named: `TelegramSettingsPanel.vue`, `TelegramChatNotificationsSettings.vue`, and the ntfy block in `SettingsView.vue`. I read each template and script, then checked the server routes they call, so each rewritten message matched what the server returns. I replaced the Telegram panel's native `confirm()` calls with the shared `ConfirmDialog` that `AuthSettingsPanel` already uses. I split a silent load failure from a real empty list. I fixed a PATCH that spread `JSON_OPTS`, a function, so it went out without a `Content-Type` header. The status line now uses plain phrases instead of raw enum names, and the ntfy test shows a result line with a next step.

Review round 1 found that the same two bugs existed elsewhere. I fixed each class everywhere rather than only the named site. `reminders.ts`, `AuthSettingsPanel.vue` and `TaskDrawer.vue` now call `JSON_OPTS(method, body)` or `JSON_OPTS("POST", {})` instead of spreading it. `JSON_OPTS` accepts `DELETE` so the reminders store can use it for every method, and bodyless POSTs now send `{}` with the JSON header, as the other callers do. For the native prompts, `ServiceSettings.vue` (remove service), `TaskCard.vue` (cancel stalled check), `SystemResourcePanel.vue` (kill process), `TaskDrawer.vue` (reopen done task) and `SettingsView.vue` (discard unsaved `repoos.toml` edits) each open the shared `ConfirmDialog` with a named action. Cancelling changes nothing.

The review's edge cases are handled too. A chat type shows as "Private chat", "Group" or "Channel", never Telegram's raw name. An unknown receive mode reads "receive status unknown" instead of a bare "· ". A stale toggle error clears when the feature is switched off. The browser test checks for the status phrase rather than a bare word, so future copy can use the word. The declared shot label names only what the capture shows, the ntfy topic row.

Tests: `native-dialog-json-opts-guard.test.ts` is table-driven. Each row scans every `.vue` and `.ts` file under `ui-app/src` for one banned form, skipping comment lines. Sample cases prove the scanner catches the bad forms and ignores legitimate ones. `notifications-settings-qa-browser.test.ts` runs headless WebKit against fixtures at 375, 768 and 1280 px, with 13 cases. The Telegram component and chat-notification tests cover the PATCH shape, the error states, the labels and the stale-error clearing.

## Approaches tried

I used the existing `ConfirmDialog` for all five confirms rather than adding a new abstraction. Each call site keeps its copy in the template, which matches `AuthSettingsPanel`.

My first browser run timed out waiting for the Telegram section. The cause was not the component: `build:ui` runs `vue-tsc` and then Vite, and a type error stopped the chain before Vite emitted `dist/ui`, so the server answered `/settings` with a JSON 404. Fixing the type error fixed the run.

A later scoped check failed only on formatting, which I fixed by running the formatter and rerunning.

## Challenges and blockers

One remote-validation run failed a single reviewer-prompt test, `agent-review.test.ts`. That test does not touch any code I changed. It passed when I ran it locally in isolation, and the gate's remote run passed on a rerun. I treated it as a flake and did not change code for it. The passing run is the one I am reporting.

Per-dialog behaviour tests for the five new confirms are not included. The guard test proves no native prompt remains, and the existing suites for those components still pass, but a targeted test for each dialog's cancel and confirm paths would be stronger. I can add them if the human wants them.

No human-only step blocks the code. The acceptance criteria are met with fixtures. Two checks still need a human: a real Telegram bot (the task forbids real tokens here) and an ntfy test delivered to a device. Those belong in a held human task.

## Key learnings

A test that mocks the helper can pass while the wire format is wrong. The `JSON_OPTS` spread would have passed any test that mocks `api`. Only checking the outgoing init caught it, so assert on the request shape.

When a review names one instance of a bug, the bug is almost always a class. Searching for the same pattern across the source found three spreads and five confirms that a per-site fix would have left behind. A guard test keeps the class from coming back.

A swallowed error is worse than a visible one, because an empty state looks like a real answer. Any load path that catches and falls back to an empty list should say so.
